Building a square

A square of size k needs three neighboring squares:
  • Check the square above.
  • Check the square on the left.
  • Check the diagonal square.
The smallest neighbor determines the next size.

Why use the minimum?

Consider neighboring sizes of 2, 3, and 4.
The short side limits how far the square can extend.
